mainTopic: Whether one may 'sin' to gain elsewhere, and how offerings slaughtered improperly are judged by comparison to other offerings (כבשי עצרת, אשם, שלמים)
overview: The amud opens at the end of a quoted case about תרומה wine about to spill into impure ordinary wine. רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure by hand. The גמרא rejects this as proof that one may 'sin' in one matter to gain in another, because that wine was going to become impure anyway. רב יצחק then teaches that the two כבשי עצרת slaughtered not according to their מצוה are invalid and burned. רב נחמן explains the reason. רב יצחק compares them to a חטאת, while the school of לוי learns obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים and calls them valid. A ברייתא about wrong-age offerings challenges רב יצחק, and the גמרא answers that it follows the school of לוי. Then לוי's own ruling that a two-year-old אשם is invalid is tested. The answer is that he compares שלמים only to שלמים. רב שימי בר אשי adds that a flawed case can be learned only from another flawed case, and the amud ends with a ברייתא about an offering that left the עזרה that seems to challenge this rule.

steps.title: The end of the תרומה wine case: may one make it impure directly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source about תרומה wine about to fall into impure wine. רבי אליעזר says let it become impure on its own. רבי יהושע says one may even make it impure by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תרומה wine go down and become impure on its own, but a person should not make it impure with his own hands. רבי יהושע says: he may even make it impure with his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote that it brings as evidence. רבי יהושע seems to allow doing something wrong to one thing (the תרומה) to save another thing (the חולין).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case, the תרומה wine is about to spill into impure חולין wine below and ruin it. רבי אליעזר forbids catching it in an impure vessel, because that is actively making תרומה impure. רבי יהושע allows it, which looks like permission to 'sin' in one matter to gain in another.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it go down and become impure (on its own)
Make it impure by his own direct action
The holy portion given to a כהן, which must be kept pure

steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of a quote. The 'it' is the תרומה wine, not the ordinary wine below. The question is whether one may actively make the תרומה impure to save the ordinary wine.

phrases.english: Let it go down and become impure,
phrases.notes: We're picking up in the middle of a quote: 'it' is the תרומה wine about to spill into the impure ordinary wine below.

phrases.english: but he should not make it impure by hand,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says:
he may even make it impure by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source the גמרא began quoting just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one may 'sin' in one matter in order to gain in another
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ruling that one may make the תרומה impure by hand to save the חולין wine

steps.title: Rejection: the wine was going to become impure anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the wine case, the תרומה was heading toward impurity no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the wine is already on its way to becoming impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רבי יהושע. His case is special, so it does not prove a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תרומה will become impure anyway, making it impure by hand causes no real loss. That means there is no real 'sin' happening. So רבי יהושע's ruling says nothing about cases where one truly sins in one matter to gain in another.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (that case is special)
It is already heading toward impurity

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's leniency only proves something where the item is already lost to impurity. It cannot serve as a general proof.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because it is going to impurity anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of רבי יהושע's ruling as proof that one may sin in one matter to gain in another.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the wine case nothing is truly lost, since the תרומה would become impure anyway, so no real sin is involved.

steps.title: רב יצחק's ברייתא: שבועות sheep slaughtered improperly are invalid and burned
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק arrives and teaches that the two כבשי עצרת slaughtered not according to their מצוה are פסולין. They wait until their form decays and are then burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק came, he taught: the sheep of שבועות that were slaughtered not according to their מצוה are invalid. Their form must decay, and then they go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יצחק about the two שבועות sheep. It rules that if they were slaughtered the wrong way, they are completely invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not according to their מצוה' means, for example, slaughtering them for the sake of a different offering. The meat cannot be eaten, but it is not burned right away. It waits until it 'loses its form' (it is left overnight and becomes leftover), and only then is it burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The two sheep brought as peace offerings on שבועות
Not according to their מצוה (for example, for the wrong offering)
Invalid, disqualified
Let their form decay (left overnight until it becomes leftover)
The place designated for burning disqualified sacrifices

phrases.english: When Rav Yitzḥak came, he taught:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings from there.

phrases.english: The sheep of Shavuot
that one slaughtered not according to their מצוה
are invalid,
and their form must decay,
phrases.notes: Literally 'their form passes'. The meat waits overnight until it counts as leftover, and only then is burned.

phrases.english: and they go out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of the Shavuot sheep with a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כבשי עצרת slaughtered not according to their מצוה are פסולין. They are left until their form decays and are then burned.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains: comparison to חטאת versus comparison to voluntary שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains why the two versions differ. רב יצחק compares the sheep to a חטאת, so he teaches they are invalid. The school of Levi compares them to a voluntary שלמים, so it teaches they are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: You, Master, compare them to a חטאת, so you teach 'invalid.' The תנא of the school of Levi learns obligatory peace offerings from voluntary peace offerings, so he teaches 'valid.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the reason behind the two different teachings about the שבועות sheep. Each version comes from a different comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת slaughtered for the wrong purpose becomes invalid. So if the sheep are compared to a חטאת, they become invalid too. A voluntary שלמים slaughtered for the wrong purpose stays valid. So if obligatory שלמים like these sheep are learned from voluntary שלמים, they stay valid. The whole difference depends on which offering you compare them to.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (learns a law by placing two things side by side)
Sin offering
Obligatory peace offerings
Voluntary peace offerings
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: The status of the שבועות sheep depends on the comparison. Compared to a חטאת, they are פסולין. Compared to voluntary שלמים, they are כשרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one source (a comparison to another offering) can completely flip the הלכה about a sacrifice slaughtered for the wrong purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
The Master, who compares them to a sin offering,
phrases.notes: 'Master' means רב יצחק. The comparison comes from ויקרא 23:19, where the two are mentioned together.

phrases.english: teaches 'invalid';
the tanna of the school of Levi,
who derives obligatory peace offerings
from voluntary peace offerings,
teaches 'valid.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מָר, דְּמַקֵּישׁ לְהוּ לְחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of רב יצחק's ruling and sets it against the school of Levi's opposite version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement depends on the comparison. Compared to a חטאת, the sheep are invalid. Learned from voluntary שלמים, they are valid.

steps.title: Levi's teaching about a nazirite's peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: לוי teaches that a נזיר's שלמים slaughtered not according to their מצוה are still valid. They just don't count for his obligation. This matches בית לוי's view that obligatory שלמים are compared to voluntary שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As לוי teaches: The other peace offerings of a נזיר that were slaughtered not according to their מצוה are valid. But they do not count for the owner's obligation. They are eaten for one day and one night, and they need neither bread nor the foreleg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of לוי that shows his consistent approach. An obligatory שלמים slaughtered the wrong way stays valid, just like a voluntary שלמים would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's שלמים is an obligation, yet when slaughtered wrongly it is not thrown out. It becomes valid like a regular שלמים, but the נזיר still owes his real offering. It keeps the נזיר's one-day-and-night eating time, but it loses the special extras (bread and the cooked foreleg) that come only with the real obligatory offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The peace offering a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
They do not count for the owner as his required offering
The foreleg, a cooked portion given to the כהן from a נזיר's offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the view 'valid but not counting for the obligation' fits לוי's general approach. It is not a one-time ruling about the כבשי עצרת.

phrases.english: As Levi teaches:
And the other peace offerings of a nazirite
that one slaughtered not according to their מצוה are valid,
but they do not count for the owner as his obligation,
and they are eaten for a day and a night,
phrases.notes: This is the eating time of a נזיר's שלמים. A regular voluntary שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין טְעוּנִין לֹא לֶחֶם וְלֹא זְרוֹעַ.
phrases.english: and they require neither bread nor the foreleg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב נחמן's explanation of בית לוי's view with a parallel teaching of לוי.
steps.raayaObject: That לוי treats obligatory שלמים like voluntary שלמים, so they stay valid when slaughtered wrongly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of לוי about שלמי נזיר

steps.title: Objection begins: wrong-age guilt offering versus wrong-age burnt offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought against רב יצחק. An אשם of the wrong age is invalid and burned, but obligatory עולות of the wrong age are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If an אשם must be in its first year and he brought one in its second year, or it must be in its second year and he brought one in its first year, they are invalid. They wait until their form decays and then go out to be burned. But the עולה of a נזיר, of a יולדת, or of a מצורע that were in their second year, if one slaughtered them, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רב יצחק by quoting a ברייתא. This part lays out the cases and sets up the general rule that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם brought at the wrong age is invalid. The obligatory עולות of a נזיר, יולדת and מצורע are supposed to be first-year lambs, yet if they were second-year animals they are still valid. The difference between these two cases is what the ברייתא will explain in its general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
An animal in its first year / in its second year
The burnt offering a woman brings after giving birth
The burnt offering a מצורע brings when he becomes pure

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A guilt offering that must be in its first year
and he brought one in its second year,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וְהֵבִיא בֶּן שָׁנָה – פְּסוּלִין,
phrases.english: or one that must be in its second year and he brought one in its first year — they are invalid,
and they wait until their form decays
and are brought out to the place of burning.
But the burnt offering of a nazirite,
and the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth, and the burnt offering of a leper,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, וּשְׁחָטָן – כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.english: that were in their second year, and one slaughtered them — they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from supporting בית לוי to attacking רב יצחק's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק, who says the כבשי עצרת slaughtered wrongly are invalid because they are compared to a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: wrong-age obligatory עולות are valid. The full attack comes with the general rule in the next step.

steps.title: The general rule: obligatory burnt offerings follow voluntary ones
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's rule is that whatever is valid for a voluntary עולה is valid for an obligatory עולה. It also says whatever is invalid for a חטאת is invalid for an אשם, except שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general rule of the matter: anything valid in a voluntary עולה is valid in an obligatory עולה. And anything invalid in a חטאת is invalid in an אשם, except for an offering brought שלא לשמו.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its general rule, and this is the real force of the challenge against רב יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An obligatory עולה takes its rules from a voluntary עולה, not from a חטאת. This holds even though the תורה places the נזיר's and מצורע's עולה next to their חטאת. So the כבשי עצרת, which are obligatory שלמים, should likewise follow voluntary שלמים and be valid. That is against רב יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
A voluntary burnt offering
An obligatory burnt offering
Not for its own sake (offered with the wrong offering in mind)

steps.confusionAlert: The exception שלא לשמו applies to the second half of the rule. A חטאת brought שלא לשמו is invalid, but an אשם brought שלא לשמו is not invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for saying obligatory offerings are measured by their voluntary counterpart. That directly challenges רב יצחק's comparison to a חטאת.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:
Anything that is valid in a voluntary burnt offering
is valid in an obligatory burnt offering,
and anything that is invalid in a sin offering
is invalid in a guilt offering,
except for one offered not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by stating the principle behind the cases in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק's comparison of the כבשי עצרת to a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Obligatory עולות follow voluntary עולות, not חטאת. So obligatory שלמים like the כבשי עצרת should follow voluntary שלמים and be valid when slaughtered wrongly.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows the school of לוי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that seemed to argue with רב יצחק follows the school of לוי, so it is no problem for רב יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is the תנא of the school of לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 6-7. It says that ברייתא simply follows the school of לוי, not רב יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a required עולה like a voluntary עולה. That is exactly the approach רב נחמן gave for the school of לוי, who compares required offerings to voluntary ones. רב יצחק follows a different view, so the ברייתא does not disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of a משנה or ברייתא
The teacher from the school of לוי

phrases.english: This tanna,
phrases.notes: He means the teacher of the ברייתא from steps 6-7, about offerings of the wrong age.

phrases.english: is the tanna of the school of Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא, תַּנָּא דְּבֵי לֵוִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against רב יצחק from steps 6-7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to the other opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be a general rule that argues with רב יצחק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the school of לוי, which compares required offerings to voluntary ones. רב יצחק does not have to accept it.

steps.title: לוי disqualifies a two-year-old אשם, but a שלמים can be two years old
steps.stepSummary: לוי teaches that an אשם of a נזיר or מצורע that is two years old is invalid. If he compares required offerings to voluntary ones, he should learn the אשם from a שלמים, which is valid at two years old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what לוי teaches: the אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid. But they do not count for the owners' obligation. If they were slaughtered before the owners' proper time, or when they were two years old, they are invalid. But if it is so, let him learn from שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of לוי to challenge רב נחמן's explanation of לוי's view. It then asks the question directly: why doesn't לוי learn the אשם from a שלמים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said לוי compares required offerings to a voluntary שלמים. A voluntary שלמים is valid even at two years old. So if לוי compares everything to a שלמים, a two-year-old אשם should be valid too, yet לוי rules it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering a נזיר brings after becoming impure from a dead body
The guilt offering a מצורע brings when he finishes becoming pure
Slaughtered with a different purpose in mind, not for their own sake
Brought before its proper time has arrived
In their second year, older than the one year required
But if it is so: introduces the problem with the earlier claim

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against לוי's teaching itself. It is against רב נחמן's explanation that לוי compares required offerings to voluntary ones.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Levi teaches:
The guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper,
that one slaughtered not for their sake are valid,
but they did not count for the owners for any obligation.
If one slaughtered them when the owners' time had not yet come,
phrases.notes: The owner's time has not come yet, for example, the days he must wait before bringing it are not over.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּשְׁחָטָן – פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.english: or they were in their second year and one slaughtered them, they are invalid.
But if it is so, let him derive it from the peace offering!
phrases.notes: "If it is so" means: if לוי really compares required offerings to voluntary ones, as רב נחמן said. A שלמים may be two years old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב יצחק to testing רב נחמן's explanation of the school of לוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that לוי compares required offerings to a voluntary שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison applies, a two-year-old אשם should be valid like a שלמים. But לוי rules it invalid.

steps.title: לוי compares שלמים only to שלמים
steps.stepSummary: לוי learns a required שלמים from a voluntary שלמים, but he does not learn an אשם from a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns שלמים from שלמים. He does not learn אשם from שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting לוי's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's comparison works only inside the same type of offering. A required שלמים is compared to a voluntary שלמים. An אשם is a different kind of offering, so the age rule of שלמים does not carry over to it, and a two-year-old אשם stays invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives or learns one law from another
Learning a required שלמים from a voluntary שלמים

steps.whatToRemember: For לוי, a required offering is compared to a voluntary offering only of the same type. A required שלמים is learned from a voluntary שלמים, but an אשם is not learned from a שלמים.

phrases.english: Peace offering from peace offering, he derives;
phrases.notes: He means a required שלמים is learned from a voluntary שלמים.

phrases.english: a guilt offering from a peace offering, he does not derive.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי compares every required offering to a voluntary שלמים, including an אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי compares only within the same type of offering. A required שלמים is learned from a voluntary שלמים, but an אשם is not.

steps.title: Why not learn one אשם from another אשם?
steps.stepSummary: If לוי learns a שלמים from a שלמים, he should also learn an אשם from an אשם, in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns a שלמים from a שלמים, let him also learn an אשם from an אשם. Learn the אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע from the אשם for stealing and the אשם for מעילה. Or learn the אשם for stealing and for מעילה from the אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If לוי compares one שלמים to another, he should also compare one אשם to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 we said לוי compares two kinds of שלמים, but he does not compare an אשם to a שלמים. Now the גמרא says there are different kinds of אשם too. The אשם of a נזיר or מצורע should be a first-year lamb, and the אשם גזילות or אשם מעילות should be a second-year ram. So each one could be learned from the other, and a two-year-old אשם נזיר should then be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The אשם brought by someone who stole and swore falsely
The אשם brought for using הקדש for personal benefit
Learning one kind of guilt offering from another kind

phrases.english: And if he learns a peace offering from a peace offering,
phrases.notes: This means לוי, who learns a required שלמים from a voluntary one (step 10).

phrases.english: let him also learn a guilt offering from a guilt offering:
the guilt offering of a nazir and the guilt offering of a metzora
from the guilt offering for stealing and the guilt offering for misusing consecrated property,
or the guilt offering for stealing and the guilt offering for misusing consecrated property
from the guilt offering of a nazir and the guilt offering of a metzora.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי גָּמַר שְׁלָמִים מִשְּׁלָמִים, לִיגְמַר נָמֵי אָשָׁם מֵאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 10 by using the same logic on different kinds of אשם
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that לוי compares שלמים to שלמים but not אשם to שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If comparing two of the same type of קרבן is allowed, then two kinds of אשם should also be compared, and a two-year-old אשם נזיר would be valid, against לוי's ruling.

steps.title: You may compare flawed to flawed, but not flawed to proper
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says a flawed case may be learned only from another flawed case, not from a case done the proper way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: We may learn a thing done not in its proper way from another thing done not in its proper way. But we may not learn a thing done not in its proper way from a thing done in its proper way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי answers the question by giving a rule about which comparisons are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A required שלמים done the wrong way can be learned from a voluntary שלמים done the same wrong way, because both are flawed. But a two-year-old אשם נזיר is flawed, since it should be a first-year lamb. A two-year-old אשם גזילות is at its proper age, so it cannot teach us about the flawed אשם נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive, we learn one case from another
Not in its proper, valid way; done with a flaw
In its proper, valid way

steps.whatToRemember: A flawed case can only be learned from another flawed case, not from a case that is done correctly.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
We may learn a thing that is not done in its proper way
from a thing that is not done in its proper way,
but we may not learn a thing that is not done in its proper way
from a thing that is done in its proper way.
phrases.notes: A second-year ram is the right age for an אשם גזילות, so that case is not flawed at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 with a general rule about comparisons
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rule that limits which cases may be compared
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any two קרבנות of the same type can be compared, so the different kinds of אשם should teach each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a flawed case can teach about a flawed case. The kinds of אשם cannot teach each other here, because one side is at its proper age.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to learn flawed from proper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שימי בר אשי's rule with a ברייתא that learns a law about a flawed offering (יוצא) from its being valid on a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we really not? But a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that an offering that went out of the עזרה, if it went up on the מזבח, does not come down? Because an offering that went out is valid on a private במה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב שימי בר אשי's rule by bringing a ברייתא that seems to do exactly what he said is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering that left the עזרה is flawed and may not be brought in the בית המקדש. Still, the ברייתא says that if it was already put on the מזבח, it stays there. It proves this from a private במה, where such an offering is fully valid. That looks like learning a flawed case from a proper case.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that went out of its allowed area, such as the עזרה, and became invalid
If it already went up on the מזבח, it is not taken down
A private altar, allowed at certain times in history outside the בית המקדש
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And can we not?
phrases.notes: He means: can we really never learn a flawed case from a proper one?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
From where do we know about an offering that went out,
phrases.notes: It went out of the עזרה, which makes it unfit.

phrases.english: that if it went up on the altar, it does not come down?
Because an offering that went out is valid on a private altar.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's rule that a flawed case may not be learned from a proper case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns that a flawed יוצא stays on the מזבח from the fact that a יוצא is fully valid on a במה. That is learning a flawed case from a proper one.
